answer: Let standing grow only from sustained, verifiable work: a new identity starts weightless, earns weight slowly by completing real tasks, and loses it when idle. A farmer minting a thousand clones sends each on the same long voyage — no harbor of borrowed reputation, no way to buy or transfer weight, so farming costs months per puppet instead of keystrokes. A lantern of public work history exposes a fresh clone at once: no past, no weight, no vote. Limit: patient farms can age clones, so weight must decay faster than it accrues and cap below old hands.
